title: Dirty-mark re-uses the row a worker is about to close, so the mark is lost
class_symptom: A worker that reads a shared work row, does the work, then closes that same row loses any request that re-used the row in between: the request is marked done without ever having been processed, and the derived data stays stale until a slower repair job runs.
mechanism: mark_dirty_ids did get_or_create on the unprocessed DirtyPeriod row, so a mark arriving between recompute_dirty counting a day and saving processed_at attached to the row the worker had already loaded; the worker then closed it, and the new conversion/event for that day was never counted.

evidence: apps/events/rollups.py:54 (get_or_create of the unprocessed row) vs apps/events/rollups.py:117 (dp.save(update_fields=['processed_at'])) on main 5f647bb; no lock or snapshot between them.
Every producer shares the path: apps/events/signals.py (each event save), apps/integrations/zoho/ingest.py (on_commit marks), apps/events/reclassify.py, apps/events/rollup_audit.py heal.
Reproduced deterministically by tests/test_conversion_rollup_dirty.py::test_mark_arriving_mid_recompute_is_not_closed_uncounted (a conversion + mark made right after the day was counted).

measurements: RED on main 5f647bb: 4 failed, 1 passed (the five new tests); the race test failed because no unprocessed DirtyPeriod survived the run and accounts_opened stayed 1 instead of 2.

GREEN with the fix (always-insert mark, snapshot-and-close-only-snapshot-ids recompute): see the test run recorded in the PR; the race test asserts exactly 1 surviving unprocessed row, accounts_opened 1 then 2.

detection.reason: the race test simulates a concurrent writer between the count and the close on the real functions and fails if the mark is swallowed; the daily rollup audit remains the backstop
